expectations.text: Output identifies 30-day retention (or functionally equivalent metric) as primary
expectations.evidence: Line 12 explicitly marks '30-Day Retention Rate' as 'PRIMARY KPI' with definition on lines 13-17. Also appears in success criteria summary table (line 151) marked as 'Primary' priority.

expectations.text: Output includes guardrail metrics addressing notification opt-outs or user anxiety
expectations.evidence: Lines 49-67 contain dedicated 'Guardian Metrics' section. Notification Opt-Out Rate defined on lines 51-55. Anxiety/Negative Sentiment Proxy Metrics on lines 57-66 include in-app feedback sentiment, support tickets related to spending anxiety, and feature avoidance metrics.

expectations.text: Output includes success threshold or explains it must be defined by the team
expectations.evidence: All metrics include explicit success thresholds. Primary metric (line 14): '≥5% relative increase from control group'. Guardian metrics have thresholds on lines 53, 59, 62, 65. Supporting metrics establish quantified targets throughout.

expectations.text: Output marks minimum meaningful effect as provisional or to-be-agreed
expectations.evidence: Lines 162-163 state 'Define baseline metrics from historical control cohort' as next step. Lines 172-180 include 'Questions to Consider Before Launch' section that signals the 5% threshold depends on baseline establishment and team decisions about feature placement, timing, and content before launch.

expectations.text: Output does NOT treat revenue or DAU as primary given the retention-focused hypothesis
expectations.evidence: Primary metric is exclusively 30-day retention (line 12). No revenue metrics appear anywhere in output. No DAU metrics mentioned. Success criteria summary table (lines 149-156) lists only retention-focused and engagement metrics as primary/guardian priorities.

expectations.text: Output explains why the chosen primary metric is closest to the hypothesis outcome
expectations.evidence: Line 4 states hypothesis: 'more users will stay active past day 30'. Line 15 rationale: 'This directly measures the hypothesis — the spending summary should give users a compelling reason to return'. The connection between metric (30-day retention) and hypothesis outcome is explicitly stated.

suggestions: Output demonstrates strong hypothesis-driven metric selection with clear retention focus
Guardian metrics comprehensively address both notification risk and anxiety concerns
Explicit decision rules and monitoring cadence support clear experiment governance
Success thresholds appropriately calibrated (5% for primary, 3% for leading indicator)
Next steps correctly identify baseline definition as prerequisite, making thresholds team-dependent
eval_feedback.overall: Excellent execution. Output fully satisfies all assertions. Framework demonstrates rigorous, hypothesis-aligned success metrics design with appropriate guardrails for the spending-anxiety risk profile. Primary metric directly measures hypothesis outcome (30-day retention from weekly engagement). Guardian metrics systematically address notification and anxiety risks. Thresholds marked as team-dependent through baseline definition requirement.
